question: What exact ReRevved guest values reach VdSwap, and which of them identify the frontbuffer presented by the supported SDK?

scope.boundary: This packet establishes the exact static ReRevved VdSwap call, the maintained SDK ABI, and one exact Xenos runtime correlation from a title Resolve destination to the first VdSwap source. It does not prove native-mode runtime execution, guest-memory lifetime, CPU or GPU completion, a host upload path, color correctness, or native visible output.

dependencies.use: open resolve, swap, and presentation frontiers
bounded device-publication and post-publication setup limits

currentEvidence.method: foreground read-only DumpFunctions.java, FindFieldRefs.java, DumpMemoryWords.java, DumpDataValues.java, FindPointerValues.java, and DumpStringsInRange.java queries for the VdSwap owner, its pre-swap command path and wait field, the display-descriptor cache producer, the nearby diagnostic capture cluster, the exact D3D resolve entry, and the resolve-destination RTTI and vtables; narrow generated-code corroboration; maintained SDK e89618a VdSwap, packet, and Xenos register inspection; and one bounded read-only Xenos resolve-to-swap correlation run
currentEvidence.ghidraResult: The canonical project identified the exact function entry but truncated at save thunk 0x827F7C78. It supplied no usable body or complete caller result.

generatedCall.result: The generated owner prepares all VdSwap register and stack arguments, calls the exact import, then retains the returned primary-ring position in device field +0x30.

sourceCompletionBoundary.ordinaryCaller: The generated 0x826ABEA8 worker holds the device critical section, calls 0x826A4630 at 0x826ABF80, then calls the VdSwap owner at 0x826ABF90. The alternate 0x82517E38 caller has the same 0x826A4630-before-0x826A4638 order at 0x82517E58 and 0x82517E88.
sourceCompletionBoundary.flushEntry: 0x826A4630 is only a tail wrapper that passes literal zero as r4 to 0x826A4150.
sourceCompletionBoundary.flushBody: One read-only DumpFunctions.java query identifies 0x826A4150 and its direct callees. Narrow generated corroboration shows that it emits command words through 0x8269CD20 and 0x8269BF40, passes 0x826A3FB8 as a packet callback target, advances the primary ring pointer, and sets device byte +0x2ABD bit 0x10. The exact body contains no frontbuffer read and no source-specific CPU completion wait.
sourceCompletionBoundary.packetCallback: A second read-only DumpFunctions.java query identifies 0x8269BF40, 0x826A3FB8, and 0x826A9C30. Ghidra truncates the first two at save thunks and the third at bad instruction data. Narrow generated corroboration shows 0x8269BF40 writing command words and 0x826A3FB8 updating pacing, writeback, and MMIO-related device state when invoked; it does not establish CPU-side frontbuffer freshness at the later VdSwap call.
sourceCompletionBoundary.result: The pre-swap chain establishes command-stream order, not a CPU-readable producer-completion gate for the frontbuffer virtual address. A native hook at 0x826A4884 therefore cannot treat page readability as proof that the source contains the completed frame.

displayDescriptorCache.producer: 0x82ABE328 copies the six VdSwap fetch dwords to device offsets +0x3A18 through +0x3A2C from device offsets +0xBC, +0xC8, +0x9C, +0xA0, +0xB8, and +0xC4. Generated corroboration is at generated/default/rerevved_recomp.79.cpp:23651-23678.
displayDescriptorCache.caller: 0x82AB9538 calls 0x82ABE328 at 0x82AB9728; 0x82ABBCA0 calls 0x82AB9538 at 0x82ABBDCC after updating device configuration fields, and reset or recreation paths call 0x82ABBCA0.
displayDescriptorCache.result: This is configuration-time display-descriptor cache population, not a per-frame resolve or a completion signal. It explains the descriptor consumed by 0x826A4638 but does not identify the operation that makes its base address current.

resolveIdentity.extent: The generated function occupies 0xE50 bytes through the next entry at 0x8269F370.
resolveIdentity.ghidra: A foreground read-only query identified the exact entry and one recognized screenshot caller at 0x8250B350, then truncated at save thunk 0x827F7C50. The generated call graph independently contains nine direct callsites across seven callers, so the incomplete Ghidra caller list is not used as reachability closure.
resolveIdentity.abi: The function retains r3 as the device, r4 as flags, r5 as a source rectangle, r6 as the destination texture, r7 as a destination point, r8 and r9 as destination subresource selectors, r10 as clear-color data, and f1 plus stack arguments as clear values or parameters. It reads the destination texture fetch descriptor from r6 + 0x1C through +0x30.
resolveIdentity.registerProof: The function emits Xenos resolve state and explicitly writes register indices 0x2318 and 0x231B, decimal 8984 and 8987, before returning. Maintained SDK e89618a names these RB_COPY_CONTROL and RB_COPY_DEST_INFO. Generated corroboration is at generated/default/rerevved_recomp.163.cpp:12758-14889.
resolveIdentity.negativeCluster: The nearby 0x826B1978, 0x826B1DA0, 0x826B26A8, and 0x826B2A48 cluster is conditional diagnostic frame-capture and reporting work immediately before swap. It is not D3DDevice_Resolve and supplies no production or completion gate.
resolveIdentity.result: 0x8269E520 is the exact ReRevved D3DDevice_Resolve semantic boundary. Runtime evidence now selects one exact destination produced at callsite 0x8250AFEC, while completion for a title-owned renderer remains unproved.

runtimeCorrelation.exactMatch: The first VdSwap epoch exactly matched all six fetch-descriptor dwords from Resolve callsite 0x8250AFEC, return 0x8250AFF0, with flags 0, mip 0, slice 0, resolve sequence 3, swap sequence 1, and source base 0xFF6F7000.
runtimeCorrelation.laterNegative: Swap sequence 492 had no resolve after the preceding observed swap. This is retained as evidence that an older descriptor must not be reused as a same-epoch producer match.
runtimeCorrelation.session: The interactive session ran from 2026-08-30 16:58:18 through title termination at 17:17:33, exited zero, left no process, and had no owner-visible problem. The isolated evidence root contained no reparse point.
runtimeCorrelation.classification: Promoted as exact Xenos producer correlation only. It proves descriptor identity and the producing callsite and subresource for that swap epoch; it does not prove resolve completion, CPU-readable freshness, lifetime, layout conversion, or native presentation.

waitPayloadDiscriminator.query: A foreground read-only FindFieldRefs.java query bounded to device field +0x2A94 and functions 0x8269C8E0, 0x8269E520, 0x826A3EB8, 0x826A3FB8, and 0x826A4150 found the two exact 0x826A4150 loads at 0x826A41CC and 0x826A42D8. The configured project truncates the save-thunk functions, so absence elsewhere is not used as closure; generated code supplies the complete bounded corroboration.
waitPayloadDiscriminator.preSwapPackets: With r4 zero, 0x826A4150 emits two PM4_WAIT_REG_MEM packets with wait_info 0x13, the GPU encoding of device[+0x2A94] + 4 with endian bits 2, a full 0xFFFFFFFF mask, and wait interval 0x100. The first compares equal to 1; after callback-packet construction through 0x8269BF40, the second compares equal to 0.
waitPayloadDiscriminator.fieldLifecycle: Ring initialization at 0x8269C8E0 allocates the independent 32-byte device[+0x2A94] block, embeds its base in the PM4_ME_INIT payload, and initializes related system-command-buffer state. Queue and interrupt handlers 0x826A3EB8 and 0x826A3FB8 clear block offset +4 to zero while maintaining pacing and callback state. This is general command-processor/system-buffer handshake state.
waitPayloadDiscriminator.resolvePacket: The exact Resolve entry 0x8269E520 has no device +0x2A94 access. Its late PM4_WAIT_REG_MEM is a different register wait: wait_info 3, register 2609 (0xA31), reference r28, mask 0x80000000, and interval 8. The function separately reads device +0x2A9C and publishes that value to destination fields +8 and +12.
waitPayloadDiscriminator.sdkSemantics: Maintained SDK e89618a decodes PM4_WAIT_REG_MEM as wait_info, poll address or register, reference, mask, and wait interval. Bit 0x10 selects memory and condition 3 selects equality. PM4_ME_INIT is separate micro-engine initialization, not a source-specific Resolve fence.
waitPayloadDiscriminator.result: The 0x826A4150 wait address and compare payload do not alias state produced by the exact 0x8250AFEC Resolve path. They order a general system-command-buffer handshake inside the GPU command stream and do not create a CPU-side completion point before the later title-owned VdSwap hook. This closes the proposed pre-swap wait as a native CPU-upload freshness gate.

destinationLifetime.rendererEntry: 0x8250AC90 is reached through the NiXenonRenderer table at 0x820471B0. For the exact 0x8250AFEC Resolve, r6 is loaded from stack offset 116 immediately before the call.
destinationLifetime.providerType: Runtime-initialized NiRTTI objects at 0x82F8FB9C and 0x82F8FBC4 name NiXenon2DBufferData and NiXenonAdditionalDepthStencilBufferData. The exact per-iteration path filters for NiXenon2DBufferData before invoking virtual slot +0x0C. The default onscreen subclass candidate is NiXenonExplicitBuffersData, whose vtable starts at 0x8204767C and whose +0x0C slot is 0x82517860. Static code does not prove that the particular object dispatched at 0x8250AFEC has that vptr.
destinationLifetime.providerOutput: 0x82517860 reads the 0/1 selector at object +0x98, selects object +0x90 or +0x94, writes that retained buffer pointer to the first output, writes zero to the second output, and returns true. The exact call then loads that first output from stack offset 116 as Resolve r6.
destinationLifetime.defaultGroupChain: 0x825184D0 allocates the 0x9C-byte NiXenonExplicitBuffersData object, copies its configuration, creates two buffer objects through the renderer device virtual +0x08, stores them at +0x90 and +0x94, and initializes +0x98 to zero. Its callers add the object to the default render-target group through group virtual +0x64. Initialization assigns renderer +0x550 from the group pointer held at renderer +0x54C; 0x8250AC90 enumerates that current group through virtual +0x7C and therefore reaches the explicit onscreen object through the same +0x0C dispatch family.
destinationLifetime.presentAndGeneration: NiXenonExplicitBuffersData virtual +0x14 is 0x82517E38. It selects +0x90 or +0x94 using +0x98, calls the pre-swap path and VdSwap with that exact entry, then flips +0x98 between zero and one. Run NATIVE-CORR-20260830-0001 separately proves that the first VdSwap descriptor exactly equals the descriptor from the 0x8250AFEC Resolve epoch. Together these facts make 0x82517860 the strongest concrete provider candidate, but they do not exclude a second wrapper carrying the same descriptor. The active selector is frame state, not an allocation-generation counter.
destinationLifetime.retentionAndDestruction: 0x82518678 releases both +0x90/+0x94 buffer objects through their atomic reference count at +4, invokes the device destruction path when a count reaches zero, and clears both fields. 0x82518E88 runs that cleanup and frees the 0x9C-byte container. This proves container ownership and alternating-buffer reuse, but not the lower device allocator's generation policy.
destinationLifetime.callerLifetime: The caller performs no visible AddRef, Release, or persistent store for the returned destination. After Resolve returns at 0x8250AFF0, it advances the iteration and reacquires subsequent outputs. Later cleanup walks the provider outputs through another virtual slot before clearing the transient renderer pointer at +0x550. Static code proves reacquisition and delegated lifetime, not stable pointer identity or absence of recycling.
destinationLifetime.descriptorUse: Resolve retains r6 locally and consumes its fetch-descriptor fields at +0x1C through +0x30. A separately proved 0x34-byte backend template producer writes the same descriptor region, but no static edge ties that producer to this exact r6, so it is not promoted as this destination's allocator or populator.
destinationLifetime.safeKey: The smallest non-pointer correlation key is an immutable snapshot of all six fetch dwords plus mip and slice, scoped to callsite 0x8250AFEC. Flags and resolve/swap epoch remain validation and provenance. This key identifies an observed operation but is not an allocation-generation or lifetime proof.
destinationLifetime.unresolved: The concrete vptr of the particular per-item object dispatched at 0x8250AFEC remains unproved. The lower device virtual +0x08 implementation that allocates and populates each retained buffer object also remains unresolved, including its exact descriptor writer, base/format/width/height values, allocation-generation identity, and overwrite or recycling policy. Static evidence does not prove that no second wrapper can carry a duplicate six-dword descriptor.
destinationLifetime.result: The explicit onscreen provider candidate, alternating selection, container ownership, and refcount release boundary are closed. Exact dispatch identity and lower allocation generation are not. The callsite and descriptor snapshot are strong operation provenance, but still forbid a persistent host mirror keyed by a raw guest pointer or descriptor alone.

abi.r3: primary ring-buffer reservation + 0x4, produced by helper 0x8269C7A8 with requested size 64 dwords
abi.r4: pointer to the six-dword frontbuffer texture-fetch descriptor copied from incoming argument r28 + 0x1C and adjusted by the owner
abi.r5: system writeback pointer derived from device field +0x2A90 + 0x8
abi.r8: pointer to the frontbuffer virtual address derived from descriptor dword 1 base-address bits
abi.r9: pointer to the numeric texture format derived from descriptor dword 1 low six bits
abi.r10: pointer to the color-space value loaded from device field +0x352C
abi.stackArgument9: pointer to width derived from descriptor dword 2 and the device scaling value
abi.stackArgument10: pointer to height derived from descriptor dword 2 and the device scaling value
abi.sdkUse: The SDK byte-swaps the six descriptor dwords, requires every named pointer, requires the supplied virtual address to equal descriptor base_address << 12, translates it to physical memory, accepts only k_8_8_8_8 or k_2_10_10_10_AS_16_16_16_16, requires RGB color space zero and descriptor-matching width and height, then emits the swap packet.

nextDiscriminator.site: The per-item object vptr dispatched through +0x0C before Resolve callsite 0x8250AFEC, followed by the renderer-device virtual +0x08 creation used by NiXenonExplicitBuffersData factory 0x825184D0
nextDiscriminator.question: Does the exact per-item object dispatch through NiXenonExplicitBuffersData 0x82517860, and which concrete device implementation then allocates, populates, generations, and recycles its two retained buffer objects?
nextDiscriminator.limits: Do not add a native VdSwap CPU-upload hook: the proposed title wait is now disproved as a Resolve-specific CPU completion gate. Follow the ReBlue architecture at the semantic Resolve boundary, where native queue submission and retirement can own completion explicitly. Do not persist raw guest pointers, reuse ReXGlue texture-cache or presenter state, or claim parity from page readability.

guards: Do not infer native-mode runtime execution or native visible output from the exact Xenos correlation.
Do not treat the primary ring-buffer reservation, system writeback, or system-command-buffer values as the frontbuffer source.
Do not copy ReBlue surface fields, formats, offsets, or present policy.
Do not bypass guest-memory lifetime and synchronization requirements merely because the ABI exposes a virtual address or a pre-swap command-stream flush.
Do not make the research manifest a title runtime dependency.
conclusion: ReRevved function 0x826A4638 directly calls VdSwap at 0x826A4884 with an exact frontbuffer fetch descriptor and separately derived virtual address, numeric format, RGB color space, width, and height pointers. Maintained SDK e89618a defines how those values identify the guest frontbuffer. Run NATIVE-CORR-20260830-0001 proves that the first VdSwap source exactly matches the six fetch dwords produced by D3DDevice_Resolve callsite 0x8250AFEC with flags zero, mip zero, and slice zero. The ordinary pre-swap 0x826A4150 memory waits instead use independent device +0x2A94 system-command-buffer state; the exact Resolve uses a separate register wait and never accesses that field. The strongest concrete provider candidate is NiXenonExplicitBuffersData virtual +0x0C at 0x82517860: it selects one of two retained buffers, while virtual +0x14 passes the active entry to VdSwap and then flips the selector. Container refcount release and alternating reuse are proved, but the exact per-item vptr at 0x8250AFEC, lower device allocator, descriptor writer, allocation generation, and recycling policy remain unresolved. An immutable six-dword, mip, slice, callsite, and epoch snapshot is safe operation provenance but not a resource-generation key. A native VdSwap CPU-upload hook and a persistent host mirror remain inadmissible. The next bounded discriminator is exact dispatch identity, followed by the renderer-device virtual +0x08 buffer creator used by factory 0x825184D0.
